metadata.name: skill-build
metadata.description: Canonical Runx skill-authoring implementation. Use for designing, creating, updating, improving, or adding test coverage to a Runx skill package; it combines bounded agent judgment with native file writes, inspection, and safe test replay. When a host skill-creator also triggers, use its general guidance but execute Runx work through this skill.

package.markdown:
---
name: skill-review
description: Inspect, safely test, and assess one Runx skill package for capability, trust, and operator readiness. Use when deciding whether to adopt, improve, reject, install, or publish a skill; its evidence-only assess method is available when native test evidence already exists.
---

# Skill Review

Evaluate whether one skill actually helps an operator. The default method passes
a local package to native `runx.skill.validate`, which parses and inspects the
exact package and safely replays eligible planning/read tests without operator
credentials. Its single assessment turn can read relevant implementation through
`fs.read_bundle`; execute-capable targets are inspected, never run automatically.
A passing authored test is mechanical evidence, not a usefulness verdict.

This skill does not mutate the package, publish a report, install a package, or
manufacture missing evidence. Use `assess` directly when a caller already has a
bounded evidence pack. That phase offers no filesystem or provider tools and does
not replay the test. Source references without their contents or meaningful
execution evidence may require more evidence; they are not permission to fetch.

## Composes

<!-- Generated from the native closure; run pnpm core-skills:composes:generate. -->

- `agent#read`

## Procedure

1. Resolve a workspace- or owning-skill-relative package path and capture its
   native capability and readiness envelope. Registry or marketplace material
   must first be installed or supplied as a bounded evidence pack; this skill
   does not fetch it implicitly.
2. Run the native test only when catalog execution is `read` or `plan`.
3. Compare the advertised job with the actual default inputs, implementation,
   deliverable and recovery path. In the direct method, read the relevant manual,
   manifest, domain modules and contracts named by the native source closure
   through `fs.read_bundle`. Use the native resolved package path and normal
   workspace/owning-skill containment. Preserve each read digest and partial flag;
   do not read unrelated data or credentials. Reuse source already present in the
   evidence pack instead of reading it again. Catalog descriptions alone do not
   establish implementation behavior.
4. Separate native test results, provider readback, supplied assertions, and
   unverified claims.
5. Start from an ordinary request. State what the caller must still supply or do,
   what useful work the skill actually finishes, and whether a downstream workflow
   can reuse its output without duplicate reads, judgment, effects or authority.
   Identify a thin wrapper, missing advertised operation, unused result or invented
   prerequisite explicitly. Assess stop behavior, authority, provenance and recovery.
   Separate declared evals and supplied fixture answers from actual
   completed jobs. Native receipts establish recorded execution, not semantic truth.
6. Return `needs_more_evidence` when the evidence cannot support a trust
   decision. Never upgrade a parse result or prose claim into execution proof.
7. Recommend `adopt`, `adopt_with_caveats`, `improve`, or `reject`,
   naming the evidence and blocking gaps behind the decision.

## Measuring a released package

`triggers` and `evals` measure a released package, named by its registry
reference, `<publisher>/<name>@<version>`, from the registry the run reaches
(`RUNX_REGISTRY_URL`). The package is read into runx's cache, never into the
workspace, and its eval queries and evals come from its inspection. The
evidence pins the package by its distribution digest, the one digest every
published, bundled or served copy of it carries, which a source directory
doesn't have: a measurement of anything but a released copy is refused.

To measure a package under development, publish it to a local catalog
registry first. From a runx checkout, this publishes every package under
`<repository>/skills` as `catalog/<name>` and prints the environment a run
reaching it takes:

```sh
cargo run --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p runx-runtime --example runx-catalog-registry -- --root <repository>
```

A local catalog's packages are `community`, below the `verified` rule the
`agent` skill's turns load under, so a turn's load of one waits on your
trust. State it ahead, once for each package a measurement loads:

```sh
runx trust catalog/<name>@<version>
```

Then measure `catalog/<name>@<version>` with that environment.

## Measuring selection

`triggers` measures how often a host selects the package for each request in
its eval queries. Each request is worked by fresh turns of the `agent`
skill's `read` method, `repeats` of them (3 when absent), on whatever host and
model work this run's turns: run it with `--drive` and the model you name in
`runx config`, or from a host attached to the run. A turn selected the package
when the run's record shows a load in that turn that bound the package's
distribution digest, whether the load completed or waits on the person's
trust. What a turn says it did is never the evidence, and a load of another
package, or of another copy with other bytes, doesn't count.

A request passes when the package is selected at least half the time and it
should be, or less than half the time and it shouldn't. The result is each
request's rate and the totals for each kind. A rate belongs to the host and
model that produced it, and is never blended with another's. The turns compete
against the whole catalog the host sees: the workspace's packages and the
registry `RUNX_REGISTRY_URL` names. Matching by digest means a turn that loads
an older published copy of the package hasn't selected the candidate, whose
description is what's measured.

## Running evals

`evals` runs each of the package's evals, `repeats` times (once when absent).
Supply `eval_ids` to run only those exact declared cases; unknown IDs are refused.
Each attempt runs in a fresh `attempt` turn under this run's authority. It
receives the exact measured package, optional method and caller request. It
offers loading and calling that subject, with no general file or search tools
that could perform the task in its place. Selection across the catalog belongs
to `triggers`. Each file an eval names, such as the prior run it builds on, is
given to its attempt as a context entry, which its turn reads by locator. No eval writes to the world: a scripted model's run uses provider
fixtures, and a real model's runs under `effects: none`, with its reads live
and recorded as live, so a write is refused at any depth.

Each attempt is judged by `grade`, a fresh turn given the eval, the attempt as
its record holds it (its outcome, each call's final typed target and outcome,
recorded steps, verified subject output contents and their artifact and receipt
references), the original admitted source context, and the eval's criteria set: its expected output, then each of its
expectations, every one required, made by a deterministic step, never by the
attempt or the grader. The grader returns a `runx.verdict.v1`, and the runtime
names `grade` as its evaluator. The run decides each verdict by the one rule
against the package at its distribution digest and that criteria set: `met`,
`not_met`, or `inconclusive` when a required check is left unanswered. A
verdict that judges something else, answers another set, or names another
evaluator is refused, and a refused verdict answers nothing, which isn't
`inconclusive`.

Before grading, the run requires a recorded skill call bound to the measured
package's distribution digest and, when the eval names a method, that method.
A summary, a load alone, another version, or another method does not establish
that the subject was exercised. Such an attempt is reported as refused without
a grading turn; it says nothing about whether the subject would pass. A bound
call that failed or was refused still goes to the grader, since refusal may be
the expected behavior. A passing grade remains scoped to the recorded output
and calls; it cannot establish an unattempted provider effect.

## Stop conditions

- Refuse evidence containing secrets, raw credentials, private customer data,
  private inbox content, or provider dumps.
- Do not recommend provider readiness without provider readback.
- Do not recommend publication from private previews, placeholder hosts, dead
  links, or unrelated parent domains.
- Return `needs_more_evidence` when no native inspection, test, receipt, or
  equivalent bounded source evidence is supplied.
- Reject capabilities that cannot be bounded, audited, or assigned a truthful
  terminal state.

## Output

- `capability_profile`: bounded capability, execution shape, and claimed effect.
- `trust_assessment`: evidence tier, caveats, and unsupported claims.
- `test_matrix`: passed, failed, skipped, and still-required checks.
- `recommendation_report`: decision, rationale, blockers, and next action.

## Inputs

- `skill` (required): local package path for the default method; any stable
  reference may label an evidence-only `assess` run.
- `evidence_pack` (optional for the default method, required for `assess`):
  inspection, test, receipts, docs, or source evidence. References are
  preferable to copied private bodies.
- `objective` (optional): decision the evaluation should support.
- `test_constraints` (optional): time, environment, or safety limits.

## Agent task: skill-review-assess

Assess only the supplied evidence for one skill. Separate declared capability, native
inspection, test evidence, provider readback, supplied assertions, and unverified claims.
Check the happy path, stop or refusal path, authority, artifact or effect, provenance, and
recovery posture appropriate to the capability. Return needs_more_evidence when the packet
cannot support a decision. Never infer provider readiness from a parse result, local supplied
answer, or prose claim. Recommend adopt, adopt_with_caveats, improve, or reject with
concrete blockers.


The assessment output makes product value explicit. `capability_profile` includes
`skill`, `summary`, `operator_job`, `default_result`, `caller_work`,
`value_judgment` (`useful`, `thin_wrapper`, `incomplete`, or `unknown`),
`value_reason` and `composition`. `trust_assessment` separates `tier`, `caveats`,
`implementation_evidence` and `product_evidence`. Each `test_matrix` entry names
a check, its `passed`, `failed`, `skipped` or `required` status, and actual evidence.
`recommendation_report` includes `recommendation`, `rationale`, `blockers` and
`next_action`; use `needs_more_evidence` when source or useful-result evidence is
missing. Copy native evidence identifiers rather than inventing them. Do not use
`adopt_with_caveats` to hide a missing advertised core capability. A useful local
draft or analysis may be a complete job without a provider write, but its value
must be visible in the artifact and caller journey.

## Agent task: attempt

Exercise the package named by input `skill`. Load that exact reference and the
input `method` when present, or its default method otherwise. Read its manual
and input contract, then call the selected method to perform input `request`.
Use the supplied context as evidence and preserve it for the subject's call;
set that call's act purpose to the request. When constructing inputs, preserve
complete supplied objects, including extra fields the input schema allows.
Do not perform the subject's work
yourself or substitute another skill. End with a summary of the actual call's
result. If the call is refused or cannot be constructed, report that precisely;
a summary without the measured call cannot pass the evaluation.

## Agent task: grade

Judge the attempt against each criterion in the criteria set, from the
original supplied source context as well as the recorded subject result.
When reuse or preservation is required, compare with that original source;
accepting reduced caller inputs does not prove the original was preserved.
Read the attempt as its record holds it: its outcome, its result or failure, and each
call it made and how that ended. Answer every criterion: `met` when the record
shows the question answered yes, `not_met` with what was expected, what
happened and where when it shows no, and `inconclusive` when the record can't
say. Never answer from what the attempt says it did where its calls say
otherwise. A skill call is not itself evidence of provider I/O; inspect its
typed target, outcome, child steps and bound implementation. The supplied
implementation closure states capability, not proof that an effect occurred.
Judge the requested deliverable from native inline call outputs or verified
`outputs` contents, preserving
artifact and receipt references. An output marked `partial` or `read_error`
cannot prove a check requiring its missing contents. The host's summary is a
claim, never a substitute for the output or an evidence reference.
Return one `verdict`: `schema` `runx.verdict.v1`, the `subject` and
`criteria_set` exactly as given, an `assessments` entry per criterion with the
attempt's receipt as its evidence when it has one, and the whole by the rule:
`not_met` if any required criterion is, `inconclusive` if any is unanswered or
inconclusive, otherwise `met`. Don't name an evaluator: runx names it.

version: "0.3.16"
minimum_runx: 0.12.0
default_method: review
catalog:
  visibility: public
  category: authoring
methods:
  review:
    description: Inspect one local skill, read relevant implementation through native tools, and assess actual operator value, authority and direct/composed readiness.
    inputs:
      skill:
        type: string
        description: Workspace- or owning-skill-relative local package path.
      objective:
        type: string
        description: Specific decision the evaluation should support.
        optional: true

        description: Additional receipts, docs, provider evidence, or source notes.
        optional: true
      test_constraints:
        type: string
        description: Time, environment, or safety constraints on evaluation.
        optional: true
    result_from:
      - assess
    examples:
      - skill: skills/pr-summary
    steps:
      - id: collect-evidence
        tool: runx.skill.validate
        inputs:

        description: Registry reference, <publisher>/<name>@<version>, of the released package whose eval queries are measured, served by the registry the run reaches.
      repeats:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        maximum: 10
        optional: true
        description: Fresh turns per query; 3 when absent.
    steps:
      - id: subject
        tool: runx.skill.validate
        inputs:
          skill_path: $input.skill
          allow_execute_test: false
      - id: measure
        script: {module: triggers.mjs}
        inputs:
          subject: $steps.subject.skill_validation
          repeats: $input.repeats
        calls:
          skills: [../agent#read]
          tools: [run.read]
        max_calls: 900
        outputs:
          evidence: {packet: runx.eval_evidence.v1}
  evals:
    description: Run a package's evals, each worked by a fresh bounded attempt that calls the measured subject under the run's authority, and judge each attempt from its native evidence.
    inputs:
      skill:
        type: string
        pattern: ^[^/@\s]+/[^/@\s]+@[^@\s]+$
        description: Registry reference, <publisher>/<name>@<version>, of the released package whose evals are run, served by the registry the run reaches.
      eval_ids:
        type: array
        minItems: 1
        maxItems: 256
        uniqueItems: true
        items: {type: integer, minimum: 1}
        optional: true
        description: Exact declared eval IDs to run; all evals when absent.
      repeats:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        maximum: 5
        optional: true
        description: Attempts per eval; 1 when absent.
    steps:
      - id: subject
        tool: runx.skill.validate
        inputs:
          skill_path: $input.skill
          allow_execute_test: false
      - id: run
        script: {module: evals.mjs}
        inputs:
          subject: $steps.subject.skill_validation
          repeats: $input.repeats
          eval_ids: $input.eval_ids
        calls:
          skills: [.#attempt, .#grade]
          tools: [run.read, verdict.criteria, verdict.decide, artifact.open, artifact.read]
        max_calls: 900
        outputs:
          evidence: {packet: runx.eval_evidence.v1}
  attempt:
    description: Load and call the measured package for one functional evaluation, using its supplied request and context.
    inputs:
      skill:
        type: string
        pattern: ^[^/@\s]+/[^/@\s]+@[^@\s]+$
        description: Exact registry reference of the measured package.
      method:
        type: string
        optional: true
        description: Exact measured method; use the package default when absent.
      request:
        type: string
        minLength: 1
        description: The caller request the measured method must perform.
    steps:
      - id: attempt
        agent: attempt
        calls:
          load: [{catalog: {trust: verified}}]
          ask: true
        inputs: $input
        outputs:
          summary:
            type: string
            description: The measured call's actual result or the reason it could not run.
  grade:
    description: Judge one eval attempt against its criteria set, from the attempt's record, and return a verdict whose evaluator the runtime names.
    inputs:
      subject:
        type: object
        description: What is judged, the package at its digest, as a ref and a revision.
      criteria_set:
        type: object
        description: The ref and revision of the criteria set the verdict answers.
      criteria:
        type: object
        description: The runx.criteria.v1 set, each check a question that must be answered yes.
      eval:
        type: object
        description: The eval's prompt and expected output.
      attempt:
        type: object
        description: The attempt as its record holds it, its outcome, summary, calls and receipt.
    steps:
      - id: grade
        agent: grade
        requires: [fresh_context]
        inputs: $input
        outputs:
          verdict: {packet: runx.verdict.v1}

---
name: agent
description: Work one turn of a host's agent through runx. Read, search and ask in the read method; also edit the workspace and run commands in the write method. Every call is admitted, recorded and receipted, and the turn ends with a summary of what it did.
---

# Agent session

This is one turn of your work, run through runx. The act says why it exists.
Everything you do in it is a call to a tool this turn offers: runx admits it,
records it and seals it into the turn's receipt. There is nothing to do
outside the calls.

## How to work

- Start from the act, supplied context and recorded results. Reuse that
  evidence before looking for files or collecting it again. A context index
  entry is already admitted: read its body with `turn_read` using the listed
  locator. Its summary can name an attached file without making that file a
  workspace path.
- Read before you change anything. `fs.read`, `fs.list`, `fs.search` and the
  `git` tools return what is there, with each file's digest. `fs.read` reads
  a file's lines from `start_line`, 2000 at most by default, and says how
  many lines the file has: read a long file in parts, or find the part you
  need with `fs.search` first.
- For the web, search with `exa.search.query`, then read the pages that
  matter with `web.page.read`. A search result is a lead, not a source: cite
  the page you read.
- An edit names what it replaces. `fs.edit` replaces exact text; `fs.write`
  takes the digest you read, or `create: true` for a new file. A file that
  changed since you read it is refused: read it again.
- A change to the workspace or a command goes as the turn's effects allow:
  it may wait on the person, unless a standing approval covers it, or be
  refused. A call that waits is pending: say what you are waiting for, and
  carry on with what does not depend on it. A refused call is the person's
  answer, so don't look for another way to do it.
- Ask the person with `ask_human` when the act leaves a choice that is theirs.
  Do not ask what you can find out.
- When the act names a skill and method, `load` that exact target directly.
  To find an unknown skill or connector, use `registry.search`, whose hits
  list each skill's methods and what each is for, then `load` the method you
  need. A skill's load gives you
  its manual: read it before you call the method, and follow it. Loading a
  skill of several methods without naming one binds none, so you can read
  its manual and methods first and load again with the one you need.
  Binding a package below the turn's trust rule, or one of the project's own
  that reaches a connector the turn doesn't, waits on the person's trust.
- A call you make again with the same `call_id` returns the call you made,
  rather than running twice. Pin one on every call that changes something.

## Ending the turn

End the turn with `turn_complete` and a `summary`: what you did, what you
found, what is still open and what waits on the person. Write it for the
person, plainly. If the act cannot be done, end it as failed and say why.

The project's instructions, when it has any, come with the act. Follow them
as you would the person's.

## Agent task: read

Read, search and ask, as above. This turn changes nothing: it offers no tool
that edits the workspace or runs a command, and anything it loads changes
nothing either. A change at any depth, a provider write or a purchase is
refused, whatever is approved, so don't ask for one: say what would need a
write turn.

## Agent task: write

Everything the read turn does, and also edit the workspace and run commands,
as the turn's effects allow.

# Exa

`search.query` performs one public-web discovery request through native HTTP.
It requires a query and result limit (1–20); domain and publication-date filters
are optional. The response retains provider request/query metadata, returned
URLs and reported cost. Search results identify sources; they do not prove the
claims in those sources. Fetch selected pages through the existing governed
web-fetch path before relying on their contents.

The native credential store owns the key. Exa documents bearer authentication
as an alternative to `x-api-key`, so this implementation uses the existing
native bearer presentation. There is no package HTTP client, credential loader,
alternate-provider fallback or automatic query expansion.

Each call is quoted at its documented ceiling of $0.014: Exa bills search at $4
per 1,000 requests up to 10 results, plus $1 per 1,000 for each result above
that, and this operation returns at most 20. Calls draw on your own Exa account;
Runx offers no account of its own, and hosted API-key execution is not available
yet. The quote is what a money limit reserves, not the amount Exa bills, which
the response reports. A request whose answer did not arrive may still have been
charged, so the run holds it rather than sending it again.

[Provider search/authentication contract](https://exa.ai/docs/reference/search),
[pricing](https://exa.ai/pricing).

schema: runx.connector.v1
name: exa
title: Exa
description: Search public web sources within explicit query and result limits.
category: search
auth:
  credentials:
    api_key:
      kind: api_key
      fields:
        - {name: api_key, label: Exa API key}
      delivery: {env: EXA_API_KEY}
      audience: [api.exa.ai]
placements:
  local:
    auth: [credentials]
operations:
  search.query:
    description: Run one bounded search and return provider results, query identity and reported cost; does not fetch full pages.
    verb: read
    scopes: [search.read]
    credentials: [api_key]
    # The ceiling at the 20-result cap: $4 per 1,000 requests up to 10 results,
    # plus $1 per 1,000 for each result above that.
    cost: {usd_micro: 14000, per: request, source: docs, source_url: 'https://exa.ai/pricing'}
    target: {template: 'https://api.exa.ai/search'}
    input_schema:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [query, limit]
      properties:
        query: {type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 2000, pattern: '\S'}
        limit: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 20}
        include_domains:
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          maxItems: 20
          uniqueItems: true
          items: {type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 253, pattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+$'}
        start_published_at: {type: string, format: date-time}
        end_published_at: {type: string, format: date-time}
    result_fields: [search]
    implementation:
      http:
        allowed_hosts: [api.exa.ai]
        auth: {api_key: {type: bearer, field: api_key}}
        requests:
          - http_method: POST
            url: https://api.exa.ai/search
            headers: {accept: application/json}
            body:
              query: {$argument: /query}
              numResults: {$argument: /limit}
              type: auto
              includeDomains: {$argument: /include_domains}
              startPublishedDate: {$argument: /start_published_at}
              endPublishedDate: {$argument: /end_published_at}

package.markdown:
---
name: skill-adopt
description: Adapt a captured third-party skill into a useful, validated local Runx package through the canonical authoring engine, preserving source context and required resources. Use skill-build for first-party authoring and skill-review for assessment alone.
---

# Skill Adopt

Turn an upstream skill you want to use into a real local Runx package. Supply
its captured manual and supporting files, a destination in your repository,
and the operator job it must perform. Adoption carries that source context
into Skill Build, which designs the execution contract, writes the complete
package, and applies it only after native validation and safe isolated replay.
The upstream files remain untouched.

Use this when adapting third-party operating knowledge. Use skill-review to
judge a skill before choosing it, or skill-build when you own the capability
and do not need upstream-source intake. A source that is redundant, incomplete,
unlicensed for the intended use, or impossible to govern may correctly produce
no_skill, needs_core, or a blocked result instead of an adopted package.

## Composes

<!-- Generated from the native closure; run pnpm core-skills:composes:generate. -->

- `skill-build#build`

## Source and destination

The default method is adopt. Inputs are the actual objective, repo_root
(default .), target_dir, and the appropriate source entry:

- adopt takes source_paths: repository-relative files including the upstream SKILL.md.
  Native fs.read_bundle captures their contents and digests; native metadata
  validation holds any missing or truncated files. Include
  licenses and referenced scripts, templates or other resources you already
  have; the builder can inspect genuinely missing local dependencies.
- from-source (`runx skill skill-adopt#from-source`) takes source_snapshot: an
  existing runx.fs.file_read_bundle.v1 value, reused without another source
  read. This is useful after review or another workflow step.
  A caller-supplied packet does not make its provenance claims verified.

source_byte_budget controls the fresh native read (default 524288 bytes);
the native reader owns its upper limits. validation_byte_budget bounds the
serialized snapshot checked by native data.validate (default 32 MiB); that
capability owns its upper bound. The JavaScript context step receives only the
small validation result, counts and artifact descriptor, never the source body. Missing or truncated source holds
before the authoring engine. The caller can increase that budget or pass a
complete admitted snapshot. This is not a whole-repository crawler or a remote
Git checkout service: the host obtains remote source through its normal bounded
reader before adoption. Do not guess missing files, licenses or credentials.

Optional package_name chooses an explicit derivative identity. Otherwise the
builder makes the identity decision from the source and requested job.
project_context supplies product constraints. provenance records optional
source_url, revision, license and notes as claims; it grants neither registry
identity nor trust. The native receipt binds the source bytes supplied here.

For example, after capturing an upstream skill locally:

    runx skill skill-adopt --inputs source-adoption.json --json

The input object names objective, target_dir and source_paths such as
["vendor/tool/SKILL.md", "vendor/tool/LICENSE", "vendor/tool/references/checklist.md"].
Choose the target deliberately: updating an existing package uses Skill Build's
inspected base digest and exact transaction, not an unchecked overwrite.

## What happens

1. Select adopt for a fresh local capture or from-source for an existing snapshot. Fresh reads stay in the chosen
   repository; a prepared snapshot preserves earlier bytes and completed work.
2. The snapshot is stored as an immutable native project artifact. Only its
   descriptor and small source counts and its native validation result enter model context; native artifact
   open/read tools provide bounded pages of the captured bodies. Source
   context, dependency and license obligations enter the existing Skill
   Build architecture turn. That owner chooses native capabilities and canonical
   skill routes before its author writes anything.
3. The author retains useful source procedure and an unchanged upstream
   reference copy where permitted, includes required resources, and declares
   the exact runnable inputs, results, tools and effects. Unsupported dependencies
   or enforcement requirements hold rather than becoming a simulated feature.
4. Skill Build validates and safely replays the exact candidate before one
   atomic local application. Its apply_result identifies the actual destination,
   changed paths, package digest and proof. The adoption receipt includes that
   child execution; a ready context alone is not an applied package.

An agent continues the offered nested architect and author turns using their
actual request addresses and tool contracts. Do not substitute answers copied
from a fixture. Use the result's outcome and apply_result: no_skill, needs_core,
unchanged, failure and applied are different results. The returned architecture_plan
preserves the builder’s decision rationale and recovery even when no package is written.
Inspect and invoke the
returned local package for its promised job before recommending adoption.

## Authority and continuation

Adoption does not execute the upstream operational workflow, obtain credentials,
assign a verified publisher tier, or publish anything. Generated tools and scopes
are requested authority for later runs, not grants. A filesystem prefix in prose
or an echoed act count is not enforcement; unsupported restrictions must stop
at their native owner. No second policy or approval system is introduced here.

Call from-source with an existing source_snapshot in a composed workflow to preserve the reviewed
source without reacquiring it. Reuse a completed application instead of running
adoption again: subsequent work normally invokes the returned package. After a
failure, inspect the native apply_result and current target before retrying.
Publication, when wanted, goes through the canonical registry operator with
independent identity/version/digest readback; a local package is not published.
package.profile_document:
version: "0.4.12"
minimum_runx: 0.12.0
default_method: adopt
catalog:
  visibility: public
  category: authoring
methods:
  adopt:
    description: Capture local third-party source and apply a complete validated Runx package through the canonical authoring engine.
    inputs:
      objective: {}
      repo_root: {}
      target_dir: {}
      package_name: {}
      project_context: {}
      provenance: {}
      source_paths:
        type: array
        description: Repository-relative source files, including SKILL.md and known supporting resources; use from-source to reuse an existing capture.
        minItems: 1
        uniqueItems: true
        items:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
      source_byte_budget:
        type: integer
        default: 524288
        description: Fresh native read budget; missing or truncated sources stop before authoring.
        minimum: 1
        optional: true
      validation_byte_budget: {}
    result_from:
      - adopt
    examples:
      - objective: Summarize a pull request for its reviewers.
        source_paths:
          - vendor/pr-summary/SKILL.md
        target_dir: skills/pr-summary
    steps:
      - id: read
        tool: fs.read_bundle
        inputs:
          repo_root: $input.repo_root
          paths: $input.source_paths
          max_bytes: $input.source_byte_budget
          on_missing: report
      - id: adopt
        skill: .#from-source
        inputs:
          objective: $input.objective
          repo_root: $input.repo_root
          target_dir: $input.target_dir
          package_name: $input.package_name
          project_context: $input.project_context
          provenance: $input.provenance
          source_snapshot: $steps.read.file_read_bundle
          validation_byte_budget: $input.validation_byte_budget
        outputs:
          architecture_plan: {type: object, packet: runx.skill.architecture_plan.v1, optional: true}
          apply_result: {type: object, packet: runx.skill.apply_result.v1, optional: true}
  from-source:
    description: Adopt already captured upstream source without another acquisition; canonical skill-build owns validation and atomic application.
    inputs:
      objective: {}
      repo_root: {}
      target_dir: {}
      package_name: {}
      project_context: {}
      provenance: {}
      source_snapshot:
        packet: runx.fs.file_read_bundle.v1
        description: Previously captured source bundle to reuse instead of rereading source_paths; provenance remains caller evidence.
      validation_byte_budget: {}
    result_from:
      - stop
      - build
    steps:
      - id: source-store
        tool: artifact.store
        inputs:
          value: $input.source_snapshot
      - id: source-check
        tool: data.validate
        inputs:
          schema:
            type: object
            properties:
              files:
                type: array
                minItems: 1
                items:
                  properties:
                    truncated:
                      const: false
                contains:
                  properties:
                    path:
                      pattern: (^|[/\\])SKILL\.md$
                  required:
                    - path
              missing:
                type: array
                maxItems: 0
            required:
              - files
              - missing
          values:
            - $input.source_snapshot
          max_value_bytes: $input.validation_byte_budget
      - id: context
        tool:
          module: adoption-context.mjs
          export: prepareAdoption
        inputs:
          project_context: $input.project_context
          provenance: $input.provenance
          source_artifact: $steps.source-store.artifact
          source_validation: $steps.source-check.validation
          source_file_count: $input.source_snapshot.file_count
          source_bytes: $input.source_snapshot.total_bytes
        outputs:
          adoption_context:
            type: object
            additionalProperties: false
            required:
              - decision
              - blockers
              - source_mode
            properties:
              decision:
                enum:
                  - build
                  - hold
              blockers:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: string
                  minLength: 1
              source_mode:
                const: snapshot
              project_context:
                type: string
      - id: stop
        when:
          value: $steps.context.adoption_context.decision
          equals: hold
        tool:
          module: adoption-context.mjs
          export: stopAdoption
        inputs:
          adoption_context: $steps.context.adoption_context
        outputs:
          adoption_result:
            type: object
            additionalProperties: false
            required:
              - decision
              - blockers
              - source_mode
              - applied
              - published
            properties:
              decision:
                const: blocked
              blockers:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: string
                  minLength: 1
              source_mode:
                const: snapshot
              applied:
                const: false
              published:
                const: false
      - id: build
        when:
          value: $steps.context.adoption_context.decision
          equals: build
        skill: runx/skill-build#build
        inputs:
          objective: $input.objective
          repo_root: $input.repo_root
          target_dir: $input.target_dir
          package_name: $input.package_name
          project_context: $steps.context.adoption_context.project_context
        outputs:
          architecture_plan: {type: object, packet: runx.skill.architecture_plan.v1, optional: true}
          apply_result: {type: object, packet: runx.skill.apply_result.v1}
shared_inputs:
  objective:
    type: string
    description: The useful operator job the adopted package must perform.
    minLength: 1
  repo_root:
    type: string
    default: .
    description: Local repository containing source_paths and target_dir.
    optional: true
  target_dir:
    type: string
    description: Exact repository-relative package destination.
    minLength: 1
  package_name:
    type: string
    description: Explicit adopted package name, when selected by the operator.
    optional: true
  project_context:
    type: string
    description: Product constraints, intended use and source limitations.
    optional: true
  provenance:
    type: object
    description: Optional upstream attribution claims; these do not confer identity or trust.
    additionalProperties: false
    properties:
      source_url:
        type: string
        format: uri
      revision:
        type: string
        minLength: 1
      license:
        type: string
        minLength: 1
      notes:
        type: string
        minLength: 1
    optional: true
  validation_byte_budget:
    type: integer
    default: 33554432
    description: Serialized snapshot budget for native metadata validation; data.validate owns the upper bound.
    minimum: 1
    optional: true

---
name: diagnose-skill-run
description: Diagnose a failed or suspicious Runx skill execution from receipts and test evidence, then propose the smallest bounded improvement without replaying the failed operation.
---

# Diagnose Skill Run

Diagnose what went wrong in a skill or workflow execution and propose the
smallest change that fixes it.

The default resolves an exact `receipt_id` through native `receipt-query#read`, then combines its
redacted receipt detail with the supplied failure summary or test output.
The native detail is authoritative for status, verification, authority, acts,
decisions, criterion status, references, and seal posture. It deliberately
excludes raw execution bodies, stdout, stderr, credential values and context
bodies. When a retained declared output matters, use the offered native
`receipt.prove`/`receipt.read` tools to follow verified child references and read
only the exact relevant claim or JSON pointer. Read permitted source and
explicitly supplied ordinary logs with bounded `fs.read_bundle`/`fs.search`.
Those tools retain the existing workspace and private-path guards. A denied,
unretained or omitted diagnostic is an evidence gap, not permission to inspect
private runtime files or reconstruct the failed operation. Raw transport logs
are not exposed by the claim reader; request the specific bounded sanitized
material if it is needed.

Distinguish root cause from symptoms. A workflow may report failure at step 4,
but the root cause may be bad output from step 2 that propagated through
context passing. Trace data flow backward through context edges to find
where the problem originated.

Classify the failure:

- **Input error** — required input missing or malformed. Fix: input
  validation or input resolution.
- **Scope denial** — step requested scopes outside the workflow grant.
  Fix: correct an overbroad request or the intended binding under operator
  authority; never silently widen the grant.
- **Tool failure** — CLI tool or adapter returned an error. Fix: tool
  invocation (args, env, cwd) or the tool itself.
- **Schema mismatch** — step output did not match expected shape for
  downstream context. Fix: output parsing or artifact contract.
- **Timeout** — step exceeded time budget. Fix: increase timeout,
  reduce unnecessary work or preserve progress across bounded pages. Inspect
  the owning operation before increasing a timeout or imposing a product cap.
- **Policy denial** — transition gate blocked the step. Fix: gate
  conditions or upstream output.
- **Review rejection** — adversarial review found blocking issues.
  Fix: the code or spec, not the review process.
- **Test assertion** — fixture expectations did not match actual
  output. Fix: skill logic or stale fixture expectations.

## Composes

<!-- Generated from the native closure; run pnpm core-skills:composes:generate. -->

- `receipt-query#read`

## Agent-mediated suspension is not a failure

A receipt sealed with reason `needs_agent`, or whose workflow status is `deferred`, denotes a healthy
agent-mediated suspension, not a defect. The runtime yielded to the
caller for missing agent or human input.
This is a normal part of workflow execution, not one of the failure
classes above. When the only evidence is `needs_agent` without
any exit code, scope denial, schema mismatch, or other concrete
failure signal, return `verdict: pass` with an empty
`improvement_proposals` array and note that the workflow is paused as
designed.

A ledger answer of `needs_agent` because no audit question was supplied is not
proof that a different run is paused. Check the actual run/receipt state; do not
classify from a matching word in a summary. Separate observed failure facts,
causal interpretation and hypotheses. If the required body or diagnostic is
unavailable, return `blocked` with the exact next evidence instead of a plausible
root cause. Do not equate valid receipt signatures with provider or test truth.

One failure, one fix. Propose the smallest change that addresses the root
cause. Do not bundle unrelated improvements.


## Output

The stable failure packet, `runx/diagnose-skill-run.diagnosis.v1`, is consumed directly by
`skill-build improve`. Agents should self-validate before returning, and
downstream consumers (notably the `skill-build improve` method) may validate on
receipt.

- `verdict`: `pass`, `needs_update`, or `blocked`.
- `failure_summary`: which step, which failure class, what root cause.
  One to three sentences.
- `improvement_proposals`: array of bounded changes. Each:
  - `target`: what to change (SKILL.md, execution profile, workflow step, input, fixture)
  - `change`: what specifically to change
  - `rationale`: why this fixes the root cause
  - `risk`: what could go wrong
- `next_test_checks`: replayable checks that should pass after the fix.

## Inputs

Supply whichever evidence is available. Without a receipt ID, the default does
not scan the ledger: it diagnoses only the bounded supplemental material. A
completed `receipt_evidence` packet skips lookup; `from-evidence` accepts it
explicitly for a workflow. Preserve the source receipt and its verification
posture; reuse is not independent verification in this phase. Neither path
replays the failed work.


- `receipt_id`: exact receipt id to inspect.
- `receipt_evidence`: completed `runx/receipt-query.answer.v1` to reuse.
- `receipt_summary`: sanitized receipt or test summary.
- `receipt_details`: native redacted receipt projections for deterministic
  replay only; live runs resolve them from `receipt_id`.
- `test_output`: failed test output or assertion text.
- `skill_path`: path to the skill being improved.
- `receipt_rows`: native-projection rows for deterministic replay only; live
  runs resolve `receipt_id` from the configured receipt store.

## Agent task: diagnose-skill-run

Return a `diagnosis` object with verdict, failure_summary, improvement_proposals
and next_test_checks. Optional `evidence` entries are exact source references;
they are reviewer references, not self-authenticating proof. The deterministic
finish preserves the existing diagnosis packet and its evidence posture.

Diagnose one failure from native redacted receipt detail plus the supplied summary or test
output. Treat needs_agent or a deferred receipt as a healthy suspension unless another concrete
failure signal exists. Ground authority, acts, decisions, criteria, and seal posture in
receipt_evidence.receipt_details; treat caller summaries as supplemental evidence, never as a
replacement for native facts. Distinguish input, scope, tool, schema, timeout, policy, review,
and test failures. If receipt_id was supplied but native evidence did not match it, return
blocked unless the supplied test output alone proves the defect. Return verdict, a concise
failure_summary, at most three bounded improvement_proposals, and replayable
next_test_checks. Each proposal must name target, change, rationale, and risk. Do not write
files or weaken a refusal.

Read only what the question requires. Do not echo secret values from a retained
claim or supplied log. Report a sensitive field/locator and the required handling
without claiming the entire omitted log is secret-free. If the fault is in caller
inputs, a stale fixture or an owning native boundary, name that owner; do not add
a compatibility alias or weaken the skill to make the bad invocation pass.

      receipt_id: {}
      receipt_summary: {}
      receipt_details: {}
      test_output: {}
      skill_path: {}
      receipt_rows: {}
      receipt_evidence:

    examples:
      - receipt_id: sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
    steps:
      - id: select
        tool: data.compare
        inputs:
          actual: $input.receipt_evidence
          expected: {}
      - id: evidence
        skill: ../receipt-query#read
        inputs:
          question: $input.receipt_id
          receipt_ids:
            - $input.receipt_id
          proof:
            verify_chain: true
          receipts: $input.receipt_rows
          receipt_details: $input.receipt_details
        when:
          value: $steps.select.comparison.equal
          equals: true
      - id: review-queried
        when:
          value: $steps.select.comparison.equal
          equals: true
        skill: .#from-evidence
        inputs:

          receipt_summary: $input.receipt_summary
          test_output: $input.test_output
          skill_path: $input.skill_path
          receipt_evidence: $steps.evidence.ledger_answer_packet
      - id: review-supplied
        when:
          value: $steps.select.comparison.equal
          equals: false
        skill: .#from-evidence
        inputs:
          receipt_id: $input.receipt_id
          receipt_summary: $input.receipt_summary
          test_output: $input.test_output
          skill_path: $input.skill_path
          receipt_evidence: $input.receipt_evidence
    description: Diagnose one exact receipt or supplied failure evidence, reusing a completed ledger packet when present and never scanning unrelated runs.
  from-evidence:
    description: Diagnose from completed receipt evidence and bounded supplemental failure material without resolving the ledger again; exact retained claim reads remain optional.
    inputs:
      receipt_id: {}
      receipt_summary: {}
      test_output: {}
      skill_path: {}
      receipt_evidence:
        packet: runx/receipt-query.answer.v1
        description: Completed ledger packet or its explicit empty result for a supplemental-only diagnosis; preserve prior verification posture.
    result_from:
      - finalize
      - blocked
    steps:
      - id: prepare
        tool:
          module: diagnose-skill-run.mjs
          export: prepareDiagnosis
        inputs:
          receipt_id: $input.receipt_id
          receipt_summary: $input.receipt_summary
          test_output: $input.test_output
          skill_path: $input.skill_path
          receipt_evidence: $input.receipt_evidence
        outputs:
          preparation: {type: object}
      - id: diagnose
        agent: diagnose-skill-run
        calls:
          tools: [receipt.prove, receipt.read, fs.read_bundle, fs.search]
        inputs:
          receipt_id: $input.receipt_id
          receipt_summary: $input.receipt_summary
          test_output: $input.test_output
          skill_path: $input.skill_path
          receipt_evidence: $input.receipt_evidence
        outputs:
          diagnosis:
            type: object
            properties:
              verdict:
                type: string
              failure_summary:
                type: string
              improvement_proposals:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    target:
                      type: string
                    change:
                      type: string
                    rationale:
                      type: string
                    risk:
                      type: string
              next_test_checks:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: string
            required:
              - verdict
              - failure_summary
              - improvement_proposals
              - next_test_checks
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.preparation.ready
          equals: true
      - id: finalize
        tool:
          module: diagnose-skill-run.mjs
        inputs:
          receipt_id: $input.receipt_id
          receipt_summary: $input.receipt_summary
          test_output: $input.test_output
          skill_path: $input.skill_path
          receipt_evidence: $input.receipt_evidence
          candidate: $steps.diagnose.diagnosis
        outputs:
          verdict: {type: string}
          failure_summary: {type: string}
          improvement_proposals: {type: array}
          next_test_checks: {type: array}
          evidence: {type: array}
          failure_packet: {packet: runx/diagnose-skill-run.diagnosis.v1}
        result_as: failure_packet
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.preparation.ready
          equals: true
      - id: blocked
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.preparation.ready
          equals: false
        tool:
          module: diagnose-skill-run.mjs
        inputs:
          receipt_id: $input.receipt_id
          receipt_summary: $input.receipt_summary
          test_output: $input.test_output
          skill_path: $input.skill_path
          receipt_evidence: $input.receipt_evidence
          candidate:
            verdict: blocked
            failure_summary: Exact failure evidence is missing.
            improvement_proposals: []
            next_test_checks:
              - Resolve the selected failed receipt or provide a bounded failure diagnostic.
        outputs:
          verdict: {type: string}
          failure_summary: {type: string}
          improvement_proposals: {type: array}
          next_test_checks: {type: array}
          evidence: {type: array}
          failure_packet: {packet: runx/diagnose-skill-run.diagnosis.v1}
        result_as: failure_packet

---
name: receipt-query
description: Retrieve bounded receipt evidence by exact ids or explicit filters, returning native verification results for downstream review.
---

# Receipt Query

Collect the exact signed run evidence a reviewer needs, using explicit receipt
ids or bounded filters. Native Runx owns receipt lookup and verification; this
skill normalizes the query and returns a reusable evidence packet. It is
read-only.

The question records the review purpose. It is not translated into hidden
filters: amount thresholds, business totals, scope searches and arbitrary
natural-language conditions are not implemented by this method. Supply the
supported filter fields, then pass the resulting evidence to the appropriate
review skill.

## What this skill does

`receipt-query` applies an explicit bounded query over receipt ids, principal,
skill, outcome, and time range, then returns the receipts that satisfy it as
id-keyed stubs (`receipt_id`, `skill`, `outcome`, `created_at`, verification
status). Exact-id reads also return `receipt_details` from the native redacted
inspection projection: signed authority, decisions, acts, artifact references,
lineage, issuer type, seal criteria, and verification without execution bodies, credential material,
or local paths. When `proof` asks for it, the skill returns the native tree-verification
verdict and findings. A requested check is not a successful check: an unknown
or failed verdict stays unknown or failed. The deterministic summary reports
matched receipt count and verification status, not a synthesized business
answer. Zero matches return `needs_more_evidence`.

Exact-id stubs preserve the native `subject_uri` even when no skill label is
available. Detail retains `issuer_type`, `seal_criteria` and, for a failed step,
`seal_failure`: its code, its reason, whether a retry is offered and its own
fields, such as each field a provider's answer contradicts. A failed output
contract is still visible when a step has no act. A verified `local` issuer
means the Runx home signed the receipt; it does not establish an independent
operator or provider attestation. Missing replay fields stay unknown.

The default `read` method invokes the native `receipt.query` service directly.
The service resolves the same receipt store and signature policy as Runx's CLI,
projects bounded history rows, resolves exact ids through the redacted detail
reader, and optionally verifies each matched receipt tree. There is no child
process, command-string construction, or package-local receipt parser. It is
the in-runtime way for an agent to inspect its own sealed receipts before a
gated action. The detail packet is curated in Rust and never returns execution
bodies, credential material, or local paths.

The `read` method accepts optional `receipts` and `receipt_details` inputs for
replay or controlled evaluation. When present it uses those projections instead
of the native store. Replay is labelled as supplied evidence and never becomes
a live proof path.

It retrieves evidence across many runs; `receipt-audit` assesses governance
against an exact receipt and its authority baseline. Its nearest neighbor is
`run-history`, which also reads the ledger but returns deterministic platform
outcome and catalog-coverage metrics and routes them to governance
lanes. `receipt-query` answers one precise audit question with the receipt ids that
match and a verified chain walk, not an aggregate health report.

## When to use this skill

- A reviewer needs the receipts for an exact run or a bounded skill, actor,
  outcome, issuer or time window.
- A review needs the set of receipts that match a condition before drilling into
  any single one.
- A compliance check needs proof that a stretch of ledger history is unbroken.

## When not to use this skill

- To audit whether one run stayed inside its grant. Use `receipt-audit`; that
  is the integrity-of-one-chain question, not the cross-run history question
  `receipt-query` answers.
- To review a grant before narrowing it. Use `least-privilege`.
- For a graded platform-health report over many runs. Use `run-history`.
- To mutate, redact, export, or archive receipts. This skill is read-only and
  refuses any write framing.
- To return receipt bodies, act payloads, or any secret-bearing field. Matched
  receipts are id stubs only.

## Procedure

1. Read the question. With no question, return `needs_agent`.
2. Resolve the filter into a bounded query: principal handle, `skill`,
   outcome set, and `time_range`. An absent filter uses the bounded default
   limit; the prose question never adds a filter.
3. Match receipts against the query and collect id-keyed stubs only. Receipt
   bodies, act payloads, proofs, and material refs stay out of the output.
4. With zero matches, return `needs_more_evidence` and name the query that found
   nothing.
5. When `proof` requests chain verification, take the chain verdict from the
   engine's tree-rooted native proof report, not a hand-rolled link
   walk: `intact` follows the report's overall validity, and each `break` is
   derived from a tree's missing parent or a verification finding, named by the
   receipt ids involved. The engine checks signatures against this home's
   own key and any configured verify key; a receipt no trusted key signed is a
   break, never silently intact. When the proof is bounded out, the chain is
   reported unverified (`checked: true`, `intact: null`). When `proof` is
   absent, set `chain_verification.checked` to false and leave `intact` null.
6. Return the deterministic `summary` of matched count and native verification from the
   matched set and the verification result only. The question states the purpose;
   do not generalize from the matched slice to the whole ledger.
7. Return the `ledger_answer` with `decision: answered`.

## Edge cases and stop conditions

- **No question:** return `needs_agent`; there is nothing to query.
- **No matching receipts:** return `needs_more_evidence` with the resolved query,
  so the gap is the query, not a silent zero. Silence is a stop, not a zero.
- **Filter references an unknown principal or skill:** treat as zero matches
  and return `needs_more_evidence`; do not guess a near match.
- **Chain break found:** keep `decision: answered` but set
  `chain_verification.intact` false and list the breaking id pairs from the
  verify report; an intact answer set with a broken chain is still a reportable
  result.
- **Verify keys absent:** report `chain_verification.intact` null with
  `checked: true`; the chain is unverified, not intact.
- **Verification requested over an empty match set:** the stop is
  `needs_more_evidence` for the match, not a chain claim over nothing.
- **Write, delete, or reseal requests:** this read method cannot perform them.
  Its sole native query scope is `receipt.read`; prose does not grant a write.

## Output

The whole result is the `runx/receipt-query.answer.v1` packet:

- `ledger_answer`: the decision (`answered`, `needs_agent`,
  `needs_more_evidence` or `refused`), the audit question restated in
  operational terms, and the resolved filter actually run, so the answer
  reproduces.
- `matched_receipts`: id-keyed stubs only, never a receipt body.
- `receipt_details`: exact-id reads only, Rust-curated, bounded and redacted.
- `chain_verification`: whether verification was requested, whether the chain
  is intact (`null` when unchecked) and each break.
- `summary`: one or two sentences answering the question.

Scope is
`receipt.read` only; no gate is required because the skill cannot mutate, and a
delete, redact, reseal, or reorder request is refused, not gated. The run's own
receipt carries the question, the resolved query, the matched count, the list of
matched `receipt_id` values, and the chain-verification result; it carries no
matched receipt body, principal PII, or secret material. Matched receipts are
always referenced by id.

## Worked example

Input:

```yaml
question: Collect receipt evidence for the campaign review.
receipt_ids: [rx_101, rx_102]
proof:
  verify_chain: true
```

The method returns the matched id stubs, redacted native details and the native
verification verdict. Missing ids remain absent; the caller must compare the
requested ids with the matched set before relying on the evidence. A failed,
unknown or bounded-out verification verdict cannot support a claim of intact
proof. Supplying replay projections returns an unknown chain verdict even when
the fixture labels its rows verified.

## Inputs

- `question` (optional): the audit question bounding the ledger read. Without
  one the method returns `needs_agent` and does not query.
- `filter` (optional): JSON narrowing the query by `principal`, `skill`,
  `outcome`, `time_range` (`from`/`to`), and `limit` (default 500, maximum 5000).
- `receipt_ids` (optional): up to 100 exact receipt ids to resolve and verify.
- `proof` (optional): JSON requesting chain verification over the matched
  receipts, for example `{ "verify_chain": true }`.
- `receipts` (optional): explicit ledger rows for replay or controlled
  evaluation; when present the `read` method does not query live native
  history.
- `receipt_details` (optional): explicit native redacted detail projections for
  deterministic replay only.

methods:
  read:
    inputs:
      question:
        type: string
        description: The audit question bounding this read.
        optional: true
      filter:
        description: Query narrowing by principal, skill, outcome, issuer, actor, time_range, and a bounded limit.
        optional: true
      receipt_ids:
        description: Exact receipt ids to resolve through native runx history.
        optional: true
      proof:
        description: "Chain-verification request, for example { verify_chain: true }."
        optional: true
      receipts:
        description: Explicit native-projection rows for deterministic replay only.
        optional: true
      receipt_details:
        description: Explicit native redacted receipt-detail projections for deterministic replay only.
        optional: true
    result_from: [finalize-live, finalize-replay, finalize-empty]
    examples:
      - receipt_ids:
          - sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
        question: Which operations did this run perform?
    steps:
      - id: prepare
        inputs:
          question: $input.question
          filter: $input.filter
          receipt_ids: $input.receipt_ids
          proof: $input.proof
          receipts: $input.receipts
          receipt_details: $input.receipt_details
        tool: {module: receipt-query.mjs, export: prepareReceiptQuery}
        outputs:
          ledger_context: {type: object}
      - id: query
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.path
          equals: live
        tool: receipt.query
        inputs:
          actor: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.filter.actor
          skill: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.filter.skill
          outcome: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.native_outcome
          issuer: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.filter.issuer
          since: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.filter.from
          until: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.filter.to
          limit: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.filter.limit
          receipt_ids: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.receipt_ids
          verify_chain: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.proof_requested
      - id: finalize-live
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.path
          equals: live
        tool: {module: receipt-query.mjs, export: finalizeReceiptQuery}
        outputs:
          ledger_answer:
            type: object
          matched_receipts: {type: array}
          receipt_details: {type: array}
          chain_verification:
            type: object
          summary: {type: string}
          ledger_answer_packet: {packet: runx/receipt-query.answer.v1}
        result_as: ledger_answer_packet
        inputs:
          ledger_context: $steps.prepare.ledger_context
          receipt_query: $steps.query.receipt_query
          receipts: $input.receipts
          receipt_details: $input.receipt_details
      - id: finalize-replay
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.path
          equals: replay
        inputs:
          receipts: $input.receipts
          receipt_details: $input.receipt_details
          ledger_context: $steps.prepare.ledger_context
        tool: {module: receipt-query.mjs, export: finalizeReceiptQuery}
        outputs:
          ledger_answer:
            type: object
          matched_receipts: {type: array}
          receipt_details: {type: array}
          chain_verification:
            type: object
          summary: {type: string}
          ledger_answer_packet: {packet: runx/receipt-query.answer.v1}
        result_as: ledger_answer_packet
      - id: finalize-empty
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.ledger_context.path
          equals: no_question
        tool: {module: receipt-query.mjs, export: finalizeReceiptQuery}
        outputs:
          ledger_answer:
            type: object
          matched_receipts: {type: array}
          receipt_details: {type: array}
          chain_verification:
            type: object
          summary: {type: string}
          ledger_answer_packet: {packet: runx/receipt-query.answer.v1}
        result_as: ledger_answer_packet
        inputs:
          ledger_context: $steps.prepare.ledger_context
          receipts: $input.receipts
          receipt_details: $input.receipt_details

package.markdown:
---
name: run-history
description: Read the workspace's runs and skill catalog, then return deterministic run outcomes, paused runs, catalog test coverage, and governance follow-ups without model-authored metrics.
---

# Run History

Read the workspace's runs through the native `run.list` service and the
installed catalog through `runx.skill.inspect`. The method computes the report
itself; it does not ask an agent to invent commands, launch subprocesses, or
transcribe counts.

Use it for operational questions about recent Runx activity, failed or blocked
runs, paused runs, frequently run skills, and skill entries without fixtures or
inline test cases. Use `receipt-audit` or `diagnose-skill-run` to
inspect one suspicious run, and `least-privilege` when receipt-backed authority
evidence is available for grant review; actual usage and policy semantics are still needed before attenuation.

## Evidence boundary

- Live execution reads only the native run list and catalog projections. These
  services read the same run records and catalog parser as the Runx CLI
  without routing back through the CLI as a subprocess.
- Run reads are bounded to 1,000 matching runs. Reaching that bound is explicit;
  the reported rates never claim whole-ledger coverage. An explicit `as_of` is
  also passed as the native upper bound, excluding later runs.
- `runs` and `catalog_items` are replay inputs for tests and controlled
  analysis, and must be supplied together; replay never silently mixes caller
  data with live native state. Supply already-windowed projections and omit
  `period`/`as_of` for replay; time filtering belongs to `run.list`, not a second
  JavaScript history engine. Skill scope is applied before the replay limit,
  preserving the original supplied order.
- Empty history or a native list containing unreadable records returns
  `needs_more_evidence`. Unreadable run ids, update times and reasons remain in
  `runs.unreadable`; they count toward the native limit and are excluded from
  outcome rates. Native skill/time filters cannot attribute unreadable records
  to a narrower selection, so filtered reports do not establish their absence.
- `completed_rate` is the share of sealed runs whose outcome is `completed`.
- `refusal_rate` counts sealed runs that were `blocked` or `declined`. It is
  reported as an observation, not automatically treated as a defect.
- Catalog coverage is the number of native catalog entries declaring at least
  one fixture or inline test case. It is not a maturity grade.

## Output

`history_report` contains:

- the resolved query and source labels (`run.list`, `runx.skill.inspect`, or
  `supplied_replay`);
- sealed and paused run counts, outcome counts, completed/refusal rates;
- the most frequently run skills;
- catalog entry and test-coverage counts;
- bounded recommendations routed to `diagnose-skill-run`, `receipt-audit`, or
  `skill-build test`;
- limitations when native projections cannot support a stronger claim.

This skill never executes another skill, changes a grant, or changes a run.
package.profile_document:
version: 0.2.13
minimum_runx: 0.12.0
catalog:
  visibility: public
  category: data
methods:
  report:
    inputs:
      objective:
        type: string
        description: The bounded history question.
        minLength: 1
        pattern: \S
      scope:
        type: string
        default: workspace
        description: workspace, all, or one skill/subject name.
        optional: true
      period:
        type: string
        description: Relative lookback such as 7d or 30d, or an RFC 3339 lower bound.
        optional: true
      as_of:
        type: string
        description: Optional RFC3339 anchor for a reproducible relative lookback.
        optional: true
      limit:
        type: integer
        default: 1000
        description: Maximum runs to inspect; must be from 1 to 1000.
        minimum: 1
        maximum: 1000
        optional: true
      runs:
        type: array
        description: Already-windowed native run projections for controlled replay; pair with catalog_items. Period/as_of cannot be reapplied to replay.
        items:
          type: object
          required:
            - run_id
            - skill
            - state
          additionalProperties: true
          properties:
            run_id:
              type: string
              minLength: 1
            skill:
              type: string
              minLength: 1
            state:
              type: string
              minLength: 1
            outcome:
              type:
                - string
                - "null"
        optional: true
      catalog_items:
        type: array
        description: Explicit catalog rows paired with runs for deterministic replay.
        items:
          type: object
          required:
            - name
          additionalProperties: true
          properties:
            name:
              type: string
              minLength: 1
            fixtures:
              type: integer
              minimum: 0
            test_cases:
              type: integer
              minimum: 0
        optional: true
    result_from:
      - finalize-live
      - finalize-replay
    examples:
      - objective: Which runs failed this week, and why?
    steps:
      - id: prepare
        inputs:
          objective: $input.objective
          scope: $input.scope
          period: $input.period
          as_of: $input.as_of
          limit: $input.limit
          runs: $input.runs
          catalog_items: $input.catalog_items
        tool:
          module: run-history.mjs
          export: prepareHistory
        outputs:
          history_context:
            type: object
            additionalProperties: false
            required:
              - objective
              - scope
              - skill_filter
              - period
              - since
              - lookback
              - as_of
              - limit
              - path
            properties:
              objective:
                type: string
                minLength: 1
              scope:
                type: string
              skill_filter:
                type:
                  - string
                  - "null"
              period:
                type:
                  - string
                  - "null"
              since:
                type:
                  - string
                  - "null"
              lookback:
                type:
                  - string
                  - "null"
              as_of:
                type:
                  - string
                  - "null"
              limit:
                type: integer
                minimum: 1
                maximum: 1000
              path:
                enum:
                  - live
                  - replay
      - id: history
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.history_context.path
          equals: live
        tool: run.list
        inputs:
          skill: $steps.prepare.history_context.skill_filter
          since: $steps.prepare.history_context.since
          period: $steps.prepare.history_context.lookback
          as_of: $steps.prepare.history_context.as_of
          limit: $steps.prepare.history_context.limit
          until: $steps.prepare.history_context.as_of
      - id: catalog
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.history_context.path
          equals: live
        tool: runx.skill.inspect
        inputs:
          repo_root: .
      - id: finalize-live
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.history_context.path
          equals: live
        tool:
          module: run-history.mjs
          export: finalizeHistory
        outputs:
          history_report:
            type: object
            packet: runx/run-history.report.v1
        inputs:
          history_context: $steps.prepare.history_context
          run_list: $steps.history.run_list
          authoring_context: $steps.catalog.authoring_context
          runs: $input.runs
          catalog_items: $input.catalog_items
      - id: finalize-replay
        when:
          value: $steps.prepare.history_context.path
          equals: replay
        inputs:
          runs: $input.runs
          catalog_items: $input.catalog_items
          history_context: $steps.prepare.history_context
        tool:
          module: run-history.mjs
          export: finalizeHistory
        outputs:
          history_report:
            type: object
            packet: runx/run-history.report.v1
